LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 7.3.1 WORD CLASSES: PERSONAL AND POSSESSIVE PRONOUNS.

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.3: Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Word Classes: Personal and possessive pronouns.
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Word Classes: Personal and possessive pronouns., part of Strand 7 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How can you avoid unnecessary repetition in sentences? 2. Why should we avoid unnecessary repetition?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. recognise signs of vocabulary related to personal and possessive pronouns for communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Word Classes: Personal and possessive pronouns. in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. distinguish between personal and possessive pronouns in sentences,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Word Classes: Personal and possessive pronouns. in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. use personal and possessive pronouns in sentences appropriately,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Word Classes: Personal and possessive pronouns. in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the value of proper use of pronouns. ● In groups, learners are guided to watch a demonstration or a signed video clip of words on personal and possessive pronouns. ● In pairs, learners are guided to identify, fingerspell and sign personal and possessive pronouns. ● In pairs, learners are guided to pick out personal and possessive pronouns from print and non-print texts on natural resources. ● In pairs, learners are guided to fingerspell and sign personal and possessive pronouns picked out from print and non-print texts on natural resources. ● Individually, learners are guided to use signs of personal pronouns to refer to people in a class. ● In groups, learners are guided to construct signed sentences using personal pronouns. ● Individually, learners are guided to write a paragraph using possessive pronouns. ● In groups, learners are guided to construct sentences using personal pronouns from substitution and completion tables. 1. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Word Classes: Personal and possessive pronouns. together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: Learner develops the skill of writing as they write a paragraph using possessive pronouns.

Values:
● Respect: is enhanced as learners show positive regard to others as they use pronouns to construct sentences to refer to others in the

class.

Link to other Subjects

The learner relates the concept of pronouns to their learning in Kiswahili.
